slides.title: What Robots Do Matters More Than What They Look Like: Task Context Shapes Trust in Educational HRI
slides.tldr: TASK CONTEXT DRIVES TRUST MORE THAN ROBOT APPEARANCE
slides.highlight: This study finds that task context, rather than physical embodiment, is the primary driver of trust in educational human-robot interaction. This is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: Task context influences trust in educational robots more significantly than the robot's physical appearance.
card.key_idea: A within-subjects study examining the joint influence of three robot appearances and three educational task types on user trust.
card.evaluation: Video-based experiment with 81 participants using repeated-measures analyses across teaching, procedural instruction, and personal-information tasks.
card.limitation: The study relied on a video-based experiment rather than live physical robot interactions.

slides.title: MuVAP: Multimodal Multiparty Voice Activity Projection for Turn-taking Prediction in the Wild
slides.tldr: MULTIMODAL TURN-TAKING PREDICTION
slides.highlight: MuVAP uses a causal multimodal framework to enable speaker-aware turn-taking predictions from a single camera and monaural audio, supporting HyECHO's goals in listener modeling and engagement.

card.one_liner: MuVAP predicts turn-taking in multiparty conversations using a single camera and monaural audio stream.
card.key_idea: A causal framework using Role-Relative Projection to map N-speaker dynamics to a fixed 'current vs. next' state, grounding acoustic predictions in face tracks.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on the new 31-hour AVCC dataset using Macro-F1 and accuracy for Shift-Hold and Next-Speaker Prediction tasks against MLP and random baselines.
card.limitation: Performance is lower in 'active' prediction tasks compared to 'silent' ones and decreases as the number of speakers increases.

slides.title: Adaptive Turn-Taking for Real-time Multi-Party Voice Agents
slides.tldr: ROLE-CONDITIONED TURN-TAKING FOR VOICE AGENTS
slides.highlight: This work introduces ModeratorLM, which uses role-playing and reasoning-augmented streaming to improve turn-taking precision and reduce interruptions in multi-party conversations, contributing to HyECHO's goals of modeling engagement and listener dynamics.

card.one_liner: ModeratorLM is a role-playing voice agent that adapts turn-taking behavior in multi-party conversations based on assigned roles.
card.key_idea: A streaming speech LLM conditioned on explicit roles, featuring a reasoning-augmented variant (ModeratorLM-Think) using chain-of-thought to decide when to intervene in multi-speaker audio streams.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on real-world meeting data (NOTSOFAR-1) and synthetic RolePlayConv; showed >40% precision and >70% recall improvements over non-role-conditioned baselines.
card.limitation: The model relies heavily on textual transcriptions for decision-making, with performance degrading substantially when transcriptions are unavailable.

slides.title: Beyond Usability: A UX Case Study on Using "Withdrawal Design" to Challenge Engagement Metrics in Social Robotics
slides.tldr: CHALLENGING ENGAGEMENT METRICS IN SOCIAL ROBOTICS
slides.highlight: This study examines how the removal of a social robot can prompt children with autism to seek human interaction, suggesting that high engagement may sometimes silo social behavior. This is relevant to RwB's focus on AI-mediated embodied learning and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: Withdrawal of social robots may better promote human interaction and social motivation than continued use.
card.key_idea: A mixed-methods RCT comparing continued robot access versus withdrawal to determine if high engagement masks ecological downsides and hinders human-to-human social bridging.
card.evaluation: 8-week home RCT (N=40) using SCARED, RCADS, SMS, RMET, and SUS metrics, supplemented by guardian interviews.
card.limitation: Not clearly stated.

slides.title: A Causal Model of Theory of Mind in Conflict for Artificial Intelligence
slides.tldr: CAUSAL MODEL FOR SELECTIVE ToM ENGAGEMENT
slides.highlight: This work proposes a structural causal model to determine when AI should engage Theory of Mind (ToM) to improve epistemic accuracy, supporting ADAM-CHAT's goal of inferring partner intent via ToM.

card.one_liner: A structural causal model determining when AI should engage Theory of Mind (ToM) during conflict.
card.key_idea: A DAG-based framework treating ToM as a resource-rational mechanism triggered by information asymmetry, low solution tractability, and perceived sophistication mismatches between agents.
card.evaluation: Not clearly stated; the paper provides a theoretical blueprint and discusses future simulation and empirical human-machine teaming studies.
card.limitation: The model's functional forms for signals and intuitive reasoning are unspecified, requiring future empirical calibration via simulation.

slides.title: Retrospective Progress-Aware Self-Refinement for LLM Agent Training
slides.tldr: METACOGNITIVE PROGRESS-AWARE TRAINING
slides.highlight: The RePro framework enables agents to self-generate progress signals through a forward-then-reflect paradigm, aligning with ADAM-CHAT's focus on meta-cognition and self-correction for long-horizon tasks.

card.one_liner: RePro improves long-horizon LLM agents by training them to retrospectively self-assess task progress.
card.key_idea: A forward-then-reflect framework using SFT warmup for reflection format and RL (RePro-PO) with composite rewards to align online progress estimates with retrospective outcomes.
card.evaluation: Tested on WebShop, ALFWorld, and Sokoban using Qwen models; showed up to 12% absolute success rate gains over baselines.
card.limitation: Uses only verbalized progress assessments and lacks evaluation on complex GUI automation or open-ended embodied interactions.

slides.title: Fast When, Careful Who: Dual-Process Multiparty Turn-Taking with Diffusion Augmentation
slides.tldr: MULTIPARTY TURN-TAKING PIPELINE
slides.highlight: This work proposes a two-stage audio-only pipeline for multiparty turn-taking and next-speaker prediction, supporting HyECHO's focus on diarization and listener modeling in hybrid team states.

card.one_liner: A dual-process audio pipeline for multiparty turn-taking using diffusion-based background augmentation to improve shift detection.
card.key_idea: A fast WavLM-based 'gate' proposes turn boundaries, while a slow ECAPA-TDNN 'verifier' confirms floor transfers (HOLD/SHIFT) and predicts the next speaker.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on VoxConverse using precision, recall, F1, and MAE; compared against a ResCNN-Siamese baseline and Voice Activity Projection (VAP).
card.limitation: Performance is constrained by boundary coverage, particularly in heavily overlapped or fast-exchange regions where acoustic cues are ambiguous.

slides.title: Co-Creating Buildable and Open Social Robot Study Companions with University Students
slides.tldr: CO-DESIGNING ACCESSIBLE OPEN-SOURCE SOCIAL ROBOTS
slides.highlight: This research demonstrates how Design for Assembly and Disassembly can lower barriers to building social robots, which supports RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: DfA and DfD redesigns improve the usability and perceived workload of open-source social robot assembly.
card.key_idea: Applied the Double Diamond framework to redesign the Robot Study Companion (v4.1) using twist-lock fasteners, snap-fit joints, and tool-free latches to enhance buildability and serviceability.
card.evaluation: Two studies with developers and first-time builders using SUS, NASA-TLX, and assembly timing; SUS improved from 59.4 to 89.4 for developers.
card.limitation: Small, non-random samples; potential self-evaluation bias in developers; lack of inter-rater reliability checks for thematic coding.

slides.title: Multi-Modal Multi-Agent Robotic Cognitive Alignment enabled by Non-Invasive Consumer Brain Computer Interfaces: A Proof of Concept Exploration
slides.tldr: COGNITIVELY-AWARE MULTI-AGENT ROBOTIC INTERACTION
slides.highlight: This research explores using consumer-grade BCIs to monitor human mental workload, allowing multi-agent robotic systems to defer communication during high cognitive load. This is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: A framework for multi-agent robots to defer communication based on human cognitive load via BCI.
card.key_idea: A closed-loop architecture using consumer EEG to detect high engagement, triggering an HTTP signaling mechanism to queue agent messages until cognitive load decreases.
card.evaluation: Proof-of-concept exploration using real-time signal processing, LLMs, and physical robots; specific datasets and metrics are not clearly stated.
card.limitation: Preliminary results only; the study is a proof-of-concept exploration.

slides.title: Multimodal Physiological Assessment of Contact-Rich Physical Human-Robot Interaction Under Varying Environmental Conditions
slides.tldr: PHYSIOLOGICAL IMPACT OF ENVIRONMENTAL STRESSORS ON pHRI
slides.highlight: This study demonstrates how operators maintain performance in contact-rich pHRI by increasing physiological effort to compensate for environmental stressors, informing the development of physiology-aware control for RwB.

card.one_liner: Environmental stressors increase operator autonomic workload in contact-rich pHRI even when task performance remains stable.
card.key_idea: A multimodal study using sEMG, EDA, and eye-tracking to decompose operator workload into physical, cognitive, and autonomic dimensions during robot-assisted tracing tasks.
card.evaluation: 12 participants performed tracing tasks under 18 combinations of temperature, noise, and illuminance. Results showed significant autonomic arousal increases with temperature (p < 0.001).
card.limitation: The participant pool lacked industrial pHRI experience, and controlled laboratory settings may not reflect dynamic real-world environmental unpredictability.

slides.title: Data Aphasia: An Institutional Counterfactual Study of the Stability of Academic Cognition Under Letter-Grade Evaluation Systems
slides.tldr: IMPACT OF LETTER-GRADE SYSTEMS ON ACADEMIC COGNITION
slides.highlight: This study on 'data aphasia' demonstrates how discretized evaluation systems compress information and destabilize diagnostic consistency, providing insights for MIMIC's analysis of societal-scale simulation and agent-based modeling of institutional impacts.

card.one_liner: Letter-grade systems cause "data aphasia," severely reducing diagnostic information and stability compared to percentage scores.
card.key_idea: Institutional counterfactual simulation converting percentage scores to letter grades to analyze information entropy, structural stability, and diagnostic identity consistency across mathematics examinations.
card.evaluation: Tested on 68 exams from 75 primary students; results show 69% entropy decrease and significant drops in temporal consistency.
card.limitation: The study is based on a small sample of 75 primary school students in mathematics.

slides.title: Exploring How Agent Voice Accents Shape Human-AI Collaboration in K-12 Group Learning
slides.tldr: VOICE ACCENTS IMPACT HUMAN-AI GROUP DYNAMICS
slides.highlight: This research examines how agent voice accents influence trust, engagement, and role perception in group settings, contributing to HyECHO's focus on engagement and listener modeling in hybrid teams.

card.one_liner: AI voice accents significantly influence whether users perceive a group-learning agent as a tool or peer.
card.key_idea: A mixed-methods study using a GenAI voice agent (British, Indian, African American accents) to examine how sociolinguistic cues shape teachers' mental models and group collaboration dynamics.
card.evaluation: Between-subjects study with 33 K-12 teachers using surveys, drawings, and video interaction analysis. Quantitative results were non-significant, likely due to small sample size.
card.limitation: The study was potentially underpowered to detect small quantitative effects and relied on a small, specific sample of STEM educators.

slides.title: WaveSync: Constrained Wavefront Optimization for Synchronized Co-Speech Gestures in Humanoid Robots
slides.tldr: SYNCHRONIZED CO-SPEECH GESTURES FOR HUMANOID ROBOTS
slides.highlight: WaveSync uses a hybrid framework and wavefront optimization to align expressive gestures with speech while ensuring kinematic feasibility. This is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: WaveSync synchronizes humanoid robot gestures with speech emphasis while respecting strict physical kinematic constraints.
card.key_idea: An LLM generates a Semantic Importance Wave; Dynamic Movement Primitives shape trajectories, and a Wavefront Optimizer aligns gesture peaks to speech stress using duration compression and forward propagation.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via PyBullet simulations across five scenarios using objective metrics (HbS, PAM, Jerk) and subjective Likert ratings from 20 participants; outperformed three ablated baselines.
card.limitation: Relies on a fixed action library, limiting its ability to handle unconstrained dialogue; not yet tested on physical hardware.

slides.title: Whole-Body Impedance Model Predictive Control for Safe Physical Human--Robot Interaction on Floating-Base Platforms
slides.tldr: SAFE pHRI FOR FLOATING-BASE ROBOTS
slides.highlight: This work presents a three-level control architecture for floating-base robots to ensure safe physical human-robot interaction and balance. It is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: A three-level MPC framework for floating-base robots to achieve zero steady-state error during human-robot interaction.
card.key_idea: Combines centroidal MPC and WBC with a contact-consistent Impedance MPC layer using Kalman-augmented state estimation and a mode-indexed QP library for $\geq 1$ kHz operation.
card.evaluation: Simulated on a 17-DOF biped and Unitree G1 in MuJoCo; outperformed PD/PI and fixed-base MPC, achieving sub-0.05 mm steady-state error.
card.limitation: Performance is guaranteed only within a singularity-free workspace where the robot maintains a valid support polygon and avoids kinematic limits.

slides.title: Self-Driving Negotiator: An interactive, verifiable benchmark for social negotiation and theory of mind under hidden intent
slides.tldr: BENCHMARK FOR IMPLICIT SOCIAL COORDINATION IN DRIVING
slides.highlight: This benchmark evaluates agents' ability to infer hidden intent and perform social negotiation in driving scenarios, aligning with ADAM-CHAT's focus on theory of mind and partner intent inference.

card.one_liner: A text-based interactive benchmark measuring LLMs' ability to infer hidden driver intent and coordinate safely.
card.key_idea: A multi-turn POMDP environment where agents must deduce latent dispositions (e.g., committed vs. yielding) from behavioral cues to select driving actions.
card.evaluation: Six LLMs were tested across three scenarios (yield, pedestrian, merge) using success rates and decision-correctness; best average success was 0.68.
card.limitation: The benchmark is text-only, deliberately omitting perception, vision, and low-level control layers of a full driving stack.

slides.title: Severance Hospital Launches Brain-Signal Controlled Wearable Humanoid Robot Project
slides.tldr: BRAIN-SIGNAL CONTROLLED WEARABLE HUMANOID
slides.highlight: Severance Hospital is developing a wearable humanoid robot controlled by brain signals, offering insights for RwB's work on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

slides.title: Efficiency-Performance Trade-offs in Neural Speaker Diarization via Structured Pruning and Low-Bit Quantization
slides.tldr: MODEL COMPRESSION FOR STREAMING SPEAKER DIARIZATION
slides.highlight: This research evaluates how pruning and quantization affect the performance and latency of streaming speaker diarization, contributing to the diarization and real-time perception goals of HyECHO.

card.one_liner: Study analyzes accuracy-efficiency trade-offs in neural speaker diarization using structured pruning and low-bit quantization.
card.key_idea: Evaluates a PyanNet segmentation model via magnitude-based structured pruning (hidden-unit vs. linear-channel) and various quantization modes (FP16, INT8, INT4) to balance model size and DER.
card.evaluation: Tested on SIMSAMU medical-dispatch dataset using DER and RTF; compared pruning strategies and quantization (PTQ vs. QAT) on an NVIDIA L40S GPU.
card.limitation: Results may not generalize due to the small, specialized nature of the SIMSAMU simulation corpus and specific pipeline architecture.

slides.title: LOPAL: Local Performance-Aware Active Learning from Imperfect Demonstrations
slides.tldr: ACTIVE LEARNING FROM IMPERFECT DEMONSTRATIONS
slides.highlight: LOPAL uses local quality assessments and active data acquisition to improve robot skill acquisition from suboptimal human demonstrations, aligning with MOSAIC's focus on skill acquisition and human-AI coadaptation.

card.one_liner: LOPAL improves robot skill acquisition by leveraging local performance variations within imperfect human demonstrations.
card.key_idea: A GMM encodes trajectories and local quality scores, enabling GMR to synthesize high-performance motions. Active learning targets missing high-quality data via shared autonomy and motion modulation.
card.evaluation: Validated via 2D car driving simulation and a real-world pipe inspection task; showed 27.31% performance improvement and reduced user effort.
card.limitation: Not clearly stated.

slides.title: Angel Robotics Launches Brain-Linked Wearable Humanoid Development
slides.tldr: BRAIN-LINKED WEARABLE HUMANOID DEVELOPMENT
slides.highlight: The development of brain-linked wearable humanoids provides insights into embodied interaction relevant to RwB.

slides.title: Tuning Agent-Based Predator-Prey Models Toward Lotka-Volterra Dynamics
slides.tldr: TUNING AGENT-BASED MODELS FOR STABLE POPULATION DYNAMICS
slides.highlight: This research explores tuning parameters in agent-based models with neural network controllers to achieve stable population cycles, supporting MIMIC's focus on meso- and societal-scale simulation of complex adaptive systems.

card.one_liner: Tuning agent-based predator-prey model parameters to achieve stable, oscillatory Lotka-Volterra population dynamics.
card.key_idea: Uses CMA-ES to optimize ecological parameters via a feature-based loss rewarding lagged population correlations, persistence, and bounded oscillations in a JAX-based ABM with CTRNN controllers.
card.evaluation: Evaluated using random and evolved controllers; results show a decrease in loss and emergence of oscillatory trajectories compared to random parameters.
card.limitation: The loss function is indirect and hand-designed rather than derived from a direct trajectory match.

slides.title: Video-Based Optimal Transport for Feedback-Efficient Offline Preference-Based Reinforcement Learning
slides.tldr: VIDEO-BASED OPTIMAL TRANSPORT FOR PREFERENCE RL
slides.highlight: This work introduces VOTP, which uses optimal transport to align visual trajectories in foundation model spaces to generate pseudo-labels, aligning with MOSAIC's use of Optimal Transport for intent alignment.

card.one_liner: VOTP improves offline preference-based RL feedback efficiency by generating high-fidelity pseudo-labels using video foundation models.
card.key_idea: Uses optimal transport to align unlabeled video trajectories with a few labeled examples in a Video Foundation Model's latent space to propagate preference labels.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on D4RL locomotion and MetaWorld manipulation benchmarks; outperformed state-of-the-art offline PbRL methods and matched Oracle performance on D4RL.
card.limitation: Performance depends on a preference threshold $\tau_P$ to balance pseudo-label quality versus quantity.

slides.title: Neuro-Symbolic Agents for Regulated Process Automation: Challenges and Research Agenda
slides.tldr: NEURO-SYMBOLIC AGENTS FOR REGULATED PROCESS AUTOMATION
slides.highlight: This paper proposes a compliance-by-construction paradigm using neuro-symbolic architectures to prevent control-flow violations in regulated industries, aligning with MIMIC's use of neuro-symbolic and LLM-based agent models.

card.one_liner: Proposes a neuro-symbolic framework for regulated process automation to ensure structural compliance by construction.
card.key_idea: Integrates symbolic process models as core architectural constraints to prevent control-flow violations, complementing neural LLM reasoning and post-hoc guardrails for semantic error detection.
card.evaluation: Not clearly stated; the paper is a position piece outlining a research agenda and theoretical framework.
card.limitation: Assumes pre-existing formal process models and faces an unsolved expressiveness-verifiability tradeoff for complex semantic judgments.
